en: Water comes in through a valve and leaves through a hole at the bottom. Hold the depth in the band by working out the opening, not by guessing.
New to fluids · the tank explains itself, equations on screen
I know the basics · fewer hints, same physics
Advance the tank one tick (10 s of simulated time)
Water comes in through the valve on the left and leaves through the hole at the bottom. The gauge shows the depth; the dashed band is your target.
The depth is the running total of what flows in minus what flows out: A·dh/dt = q_in − q_out.
{click} VALVE in the dock. The drawer has the opening, the flows in litres per second, and the equation behind them.
You will set the opening there, and see what it does to q_in and the depth the tank settles at.
Drag the slider, or use the +10 % and +1 % buttons. The stream into the tank gets thicker.
Inflow is proportional to the opening: q_in = opening × q_max.
Let time pass and hold the band
Press {tick}. Keep the depth inside the dashed band for 3 ticks in a row. Watch the jet: the deeper the water, the farther it shoots.
Outflow grows with √h, so one fixed valve always settles at one depth: where q_in = q_out.
